title: Best Zignal Labs Alternatives for Crisis-Ready Teams in 2026
summary: Zignal Labs was acquired by ICE and now serves national security, not brand crisis teams. Compare 7 real alternatives for crisis-ready brand teams in 2026.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Zignal Labs was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) in October 2025 and has fully pivoted to national-security intelligence — it no longer serves brand, PR, or consumer crisis-monitoring customers as of 2026. Signal AI, Onclusive, Meltwater, Brandwatch, and Cision are the live alternatives for brand-side crisis teams, Dataminr is the closest match for teams whose real need is security or OSINT, and Syncly Social is the video-native option for catching untagged reputation-risk signals that keyword-based tools structurally miss.


"Zignal Labs alternatives" is a search built on a company that no longer competes in this market. The vendor that comms and PR teams once evaluated for brand-crisis monitoring was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange in October 2025, and its current homepage doesn't mention brands, PR, or corporate comms anywhere on it.


That matters because most people searching this term don't know it happened yet. They're comparing tools for the same job Zignal Labs used to do — catching a brand crisis early across social and news — without realizing the company itself walked away from that job. Get the category confused and you either end up evaluating a defense-intelligence platform that will never sell to a marketing team, or you miss that the real competitive set has shifted entirely toward Signal AI, Onclusive, Meltwater, and a handful of others. This piece covers what actually happened to Zignal Labs, what (if anything) is left for brand teams, how pricing compares across the vendors still in this market, and which one fits a genuinely crisis-ready team depending on whether the job is brand reputation or physical/security risk.


## What Is Zignal Labs Actually Good At Today, and Has the Company Changed?


Zignal Labs no longer sells to brand, PR, or consumer crisis-monitoring teams at all. Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE — the company that also owns the New York Stock Exchange) acquired Zignal Labs on October 29, 2025, for an undisclosed amount, folding its real-time intelligence capability into ICE's data and market-infrastructure business (Source:[Signalbase — Zignal Labs Acquired by ICE, 2025](https://www.trysignalbase.com/news/acquisitions/zignal-labs-acquired-by-ice-acquisition) ).


Zignal Labs' own homepage, checked live, now positions the company exclusively as "Agentic Intelligence for National Security," organized around three pillars — People, Places, Position — built for government, defense, and protective-intelligence buyers. There's no mention anywhere on the current site of brand management, PR, or consumer crisis communications, and the only call to action is a demo request (Source:[Zignal Labs homepage, 2026](https://zignallabs.com/) ). On May 18, 2026, the company launched "Zignal AI" at SOF Week, a Special Operations Forces industry conference, framed explicitly for "mission systems, partners, and agent-driven workflows" (Source:[GlobeNewswire, May 18, 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/18/3296553/0/en/zignal-labs-launches-zignal-ai-to-deliver-structured-intelligence-for-mission-systems-partners-and-agent-driven-workflows.html) ). In July 2026, it added a partnership with Reality Defender to expand "protective intelligence capabilities" for personnel and facility protection (Source:[GlobeNewswire, July 13, 2026](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/13/3326120/0/en/zignal-labs-expands-protective-intelligence-capabilities-through-strategic-partnership-with-reality-defender.html) ).


This pivot didn't start with the ICE acquisition. Zignal's shift toward government and defense work dates back to 2021, including a $5.7 million, five-year contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — a federal agency, and a different "ICE" from the acquirer — for social-media-surveillance capability reported in 2025, plus reported tactical-intelligence support to the Israel Defense Forces during the Gaza conflict (Source:[Wikipedia — Zignal Labs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zignal_Labs) ). The acquisition confirmed a direction the company had already been moving in for years.


Third-party review sites like G2 still list the older commercial product, "Zignal Enterprise," which historically processed over 8 billion social media posts per day across 100+ languages for brand and competitor narrative monitoring (Source:[G2 — Zignal Labs Reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/zignal-labs/reviews) ). That's the version of Zignal Labs most "alternatives" content on the web is still comparing against — a product that, based on the company's own current marketing, no longer represents what Zignal Labs sells.


## How Deep Was Zignal Labs' Crisis Monitoring, and What's Left for Brand Teams Today?


Effectively nothing. Zignal Labs' current homepage offers no self-serve signup, no product name matching its old commercial tier, and only a "Request a Demo" call to action aimed squarely at national-security buyers — there's no confirmed path for a brand or PR team to purchase any version of the tool today.


**Protective intelligence** : real-time monitoring built to detect physical, cyber, and geopolitical threats to people, facilities, and operations — a category built for government and enterprise security teams, distinct from brand or PR media intelligence, which tracks reputation, sentiment, and narrative across news and social content, and distinct again from video-native social listening, which analyzes what's said and shown inside social video content specifically.


That three-way distinction matters because "crisis-ready" gets used loosely across all three categories, and they solve genuinely different problems. A brand team worried about a product-defect video going viral on TikTok has almost nothing in common with a security team worried about a facility threat, even though both might describe themselves as needing "crisis intelligence." Zignal Labs used to straddle the first category; today it's fully in the second, alongside vendors like Dataminr.


For the brand-crisis side of that gap, the baseline stakes haven't changed: roughly 96% of brand crises spread internationally within 24 hours, and brands that respond within two hours see 61% better sentiment recovery (Source:[SurveySparrow, 2026](https://surveysparrow.com/blog/social-media-crisis-management/) ). About 97% of TikTok videos mentioning a brand never tag the official account at all, and roughly half never mention the brand in caption text either (Source:[Brand24, 2026](https://brand24.com/blog/tiktok-monitoring-tools/) ) — meaning a keyword- or caption-only monitoring tool misses the majority of that signal before a team even knows there's a fire to put out (see our[TikTok crisis-listening checklist](https://syncly.app/blog/tiktok-crisis-listening-checklist-beauty-brands) for the full breakdown). None of the alternatives below fully solve for both the video-detection gap and enterprise-grade crisis workflow in one tool, which is worth knowing before you commit to one platform as a full replacement for what Zignal Labs used to offer.


## How Does Pricing Compare Across the Real Alternatives?


It splits into three pricing tiers depending on which category you actually need, and none of it is cheap. Legacy third-party estimates for Zignal Enterprise put it around $25,000/year entry, with typical enterprise range $50,000–$150,000+/year (Source:[ITQlick — Zignal Labs Pricing 2026](https://www.itqlick.com/zignal-labs/pricing) ) — but treat that as historical only, since it's unclear any brand-facing tier still exists to buy.


Among the vendors still actively selling brand/PR crisis intelligence, Signal AI raised $165 million in September 2025 specifically "to redefine risk and reputation intelligence," with named customers including Diageo, NetApp, Volvo, Bloomberg, and Uber (Source:[SiliconANGLE, Sept 24, 2025](https://siliconangle.com/2025/09/24/signal-ai-lands-165m-redefine-risk-reputation-intelligence/) ). Its real contracts average around $21,000/year, ranging roughly $9,000–$38,000/year (Source:[Vendr — Signal AI Pricing](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/signal-ai) ). Onclusive's self-serve entry floor for its Onclusive Social product runs around €15,000/year (Source:[Capterra, 2026](https://www.capterra.com/p/221928/Digimind/) ), while Meltwater spans roughly $6,000 to $150,000+/year with 12-month minimum contracts and no free trial. Dataminr, the security/OSINT-side comparison, publishes no pricing at all and sells enterprise-only by quote. Brandwatch and Cision sit in similar enterprise, quote-only territory — Cision's median real contract runs $12,625/year across 107 tracked deals (Source:[Vendr Marketplace — Cision, 2026](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/cision) ), though its parent company disclosed credit-distress signals in late 2024 worth weighing separately.

## Which Alternative Fits a Crisis-Ready Team — Brand/PR vs. Security/OSINT?


It depends entirely on what "crisis-ready" means for your team, and that's the exact confusion this search term inherited from Zignal Labs' old positioning. If your team's job is brand reputation and media narrative, Signal AI is the closest direct match to what Zignal Labs used to be, purpose-built and freshly funded specifically for risk and reputation intelligence.[Meltwater](https://syncly.app/blog/meltwater-alternatives) is the strongest option if genuine video transcription across TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram matters alongside PR workflow tooling. Onclusive and[Brandwatch](https://syncly.app/blog/brandwatch-alternatives-for) suit teams that want broader media-intelligence or historical-data depth over a video-first feature set, and Cision remains a legitimate PR-crisis tool if you can look past its parent company's financial situation.


If your team's actual job is physical security, facility protection, or operational-resilience threat detection — the job Zignal Labs itself moved into —[Dataminr](https://www.dataminr.com/products/corporate-security/) is the closer match, not any of the brand-facing tools above. It's real-time public-signal alerting built around protecting people and places, not brand sentiment.


[Syncly Social](https://syncly.app/social) isn't a replacement for either category, and it shouldn't be positioned as one. It has no dark web monitoring, no physical security intelligence, and no personnel or facility protection capability — it's not competing with Dataminr, and it's not trying to be a full crisis command center like Meltwater or Signal AI. What it does specifically is catch the[untagged, spoken, and visual reputation-risk signals](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) inside TikTok, Reels, and Shorts content that keyword- and caption-based tools structurally can't see —[social listening](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) and[competitor analysis](https://syncly.app/social/solution/competitor-analysis) built for the video era specifically. Most teams running a real crisis-response program would pair it with a PR/media-intelligence tool from the table above, not replace one with the other.


## Key Takeaways


-


Zignal Labs was acquired by Intercontinental Exchange in October 2025 and has fully pivoted to national-security intelligence — it no longer serves brand, PR, or consumer crisis-monitoring customers.


-


Zignal's current homepage offers no self-serve signup and no product matching its old commercial tier — any brand-side use of "Zignal Labs" today should be treated as historical, not current.


-


"Crisis-ready" spans three distinct categories — protective intelligence, brand/PR media intelligence, and video-native social listening — and no single tool in this comparison fully covers all three.


-


Signal AI ($165M raised, Sept 2025) is the closest direct match to Zignal's old brand-crisis positioning; Dataminr is the closest match if the real need is physical security or OSINT.


-


About 97% of TikTok videos mentioning a brand never tag the official account, meaning keyword- and caption-only crisis tools miss most of the video-based signal by design.


## The Verdict


Zignal Labs earned its old reputation in brand-crisis monitoring, but that company doesn't exist anymore — it's now a national-security intelligence vendor with zero interest in selling to marketing or comms teams. Anyone still comparing "Zignal Labs alternatives" for a brand-crisis use case is really choosing between Signal AI, Onclusive, Meltwater, Brandwatch, and Cision, depending on budget and whether video coverage matters, or Dataminr if the actual job has shifted toward physical security. None of them, on their own, catch everything a crisis-ready team needs to see — the video-based blind spot is real regardless of which enterprise platform you pick.
